summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and multiple prior surgeries was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, headache, and bilateral eye swelling. Initial imaging ruled out small bowel obstruction, pulmonary embolism, and recurrent SVC syndrome. Abdominal symptoms were attributed to pseudo-obstruction, likely exacerbated by recent re-initiation of methotrexate. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and an NG tube that drained over 2.5 liters. The NG tube was eventually removed as she improved. Methotrexate was discontinued due to suspected contribution to symptoms. Chest pain was deemed non-cardiac, and lung nodules with ground-glass opacities were determined to be stable and chronic after pulmonology review. Eye swelling resolved spontaneously. She advanced to a soft diet, passed gas, and had a bowel movement prior to discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition on her baseline medications with follow-up arranged with PCP, GI, and pulmonology.
